standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the description of the values of the left adjoint as a quotient of direct sums of copies of the generator, which is what the kernel computation uses.

standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the object U and the fact that it is a generator of the Grothendieck abelian category

standard_prerequisites.name: AB5 and exact filtered colimits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the AB5 axiom for a Grothendieck abelian category
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that filtered colimits are exact, which is what turns the verification for finite index subsets into the general statement.

core_obligations: Testing on the generator (proof lines 2838-2855): for a map into a finite direct sum whose composite to the target vanishes, the author shows that the composite to the value of the left adjoint already vanishes, using that the corresponding element maps to zero in the argument of the functor and that the original map is injective.

The kernel comparison (proof lines 2855-2862): because the generator detects vanishing composites, the kernel of the composite through the left adjoint equals the kernel of the map to the left adjoint, which is the first displayed equality.

Passing to the general presentation (proof lines 2863-2874): choosing a surjection onto the module from a direct sum of copies of the ring and the corresponding surjection from a direct sum of copies of the generator, injectivity is reduced to the equality of two subobjects of that direct sum, which is then verified by writing the direct sum as the filtered colimit of its finite subsums and using exactness of filtered colimits together with the finite case.
proof_roadmap: Test vanishing of a composite on the generator to get the finite case.
Choose a presentation of the module and reduce injectivity to an equality of kernels on a direct sum.
Write that direct sum as a filtered colimit of finite subsums and use AB5.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the adjoint of an injective map into a value of the Gabriel-Popescu functor is again injective (statement lines 2830-2834). The proof is a complete argument: the author first tests composites on the generator to obtain the equality of the two kernels in the finite case (proof lines 2838-2862); then, choosing a presentation of the module by copies of the ring, injectivity is reduced to the equality of two subobjects of a direct sum of copies of the generator, which is verified by expressing that direct sum as the filtered colimit of its finite subsums and using exactness of filtered colimits together with the finite case (proof lines 2863-2874). The non-formal content is the reduction to the presentation and the filtered colimit argument. The claim is H2.
